# Pricing

The free list comes first, and it is the longest section on this page. That ordering is
deliberate: a pricing page that opens with tiers and buries the free tier is optimised for
conversion, and this one is optimised for someone deciding whether to trust the project.

## Everything below is free forever

32 capabilities, generated from
[`boundary.yaml`](https://github.com/lgreene03/gravix-dashboards/blob/main/docs/oss/boundary.yaml).
The dedicated [What stays free](what-stays-free.md) page carries the same list.

### The product itself

- **Dashboard** — A monitoring tool you cannot look at is not a monitoring tool.
- **Dashboard lineage panel and the lineage API** — Provenance behind a paywall is not provenance. The whole claim is that a Gravix number can be checked by the person reading it, and a version of the product where only paying users can check is a version where nobody can trust the free one. Charter §7.4 additionally forbids upsell UI in this dashboard, which is tested.
- **Deterministic recompute of derived metrics** — Recomputability is docs/00-system-truth.md §4 and the centre of the competitive thesis. Gating it would leave the free tier reporting numbers it cannot prove.
- **DuckDB and Trino query engines with the Cube semantic layer** — Reading your own data is not a premium feature.
- **Fact schema validation and cardinality budget** — Cardinality enforcement is what makes cost predictable; gating it would sell correctness.
- **Go, Python and Node SDKs** — SDKs are the adoption funnel; any friction on them is self-harm.
- **HTTP fact ingestion** — Getting data in is the product; without it nothing else exists.
- **Helm chart and docker-compose stacks** — Running it in production is the point of self-hosting.
- **Idempotency keys and content digests for derived metrics** — A manifest is how a user proves two files describe the same window and whether the contents changed. Gating it would make the free tier unable to check its own numbers.
- **Late-arrival classification and partition revisions** — A bucket whose value changes without saying so is a correctness defect. Telling a user their number was revised is not a premium service, and a free tier that hid it would be reporting numbers it cannot stand behind.
- **Local disk and S3 object storage** — Your data on your disk. Charter §2.1 Storage row.
- **Mergeable quantile sketches for correct percentiles** — This fixes a wrong number. Charging for a correct percentile while the free tier reports one that can be 62% out is the definition of crippleware.
- **Minute-level rollup and aggregation** — Derived metrics are the product's output.
- **OTLP metrics-subset ingestion** — Interoperability with an existing stack is how adoption happens at all.
- **Parquet compaction and retention** — Operating your own storage sanely is not a premium concern.
- **Provenance from any number back to its source facts** — Being able to ask "why is this number what it is" is the product's central claim. A free tier that could show numbers but not justify them would be selling the part that is easy and charging for the part that matters.
- **Retroactive percentiles and dimensions with historical backfill** — This is the capability the competitive thesis is built on — the thing Prometheus and hosted platforms cannot do because they discarded the raw observation. Gating it would sell the one advantage the architecture actually buys.
- **SLOs, error budgets and burn-rate alerting** — Charter §7.3 Q1 answers yes: a ten-person team monitoring its own services considers error budgets table stakes, not a premium extra. A free tier that can show you an error rate but not how much of the month it has cost you is a demo of a monitoring product rather than one. The engine reads the same minute buckets the dashboard does and adds no write path, so there is nothing here that could be gated without gating the data.
- **Terraform provider** — Automation drives adoption and costs us nothing to give away.
- **The correctness test suite** — The tests that prove Gravix's numbers are right cannot be a paid add-on. A free tier whose correctness is unverifiable is not a free tier of a correctness product — and the Crippleware Test's second question, does gating it affect accuracy, answers itself when the thing being gated IS the accuracy check.
- **The public "prove it" demonstration** — Charter §7.3 Q5 answers yes: gating this would be gating it for money and nothing else. A demonstration of correctness that only paying users can run proves nothing to the people deciding whether to trust us, which is the entire audience for it. It composes what the rest of Phase 8 built and adds no capability of its own, so there is nothing here to sell.
- **Threshold alerting and notification channels** — Charter §4 permits alerting evaluable from batch facts; it shipped open in Phase 2.
- **Versioned metric contract registry** — A metric whose definition is not published cannot be verified, so gating the registry would gate correctness itself. It is also where undisclosed approximations are forced into the open, which is the opposite of a premium feature.
- **Windowed percentile API merging stored sketches** — The only place a percentile spanning more than one bucket can be answered correctly, because the semantic layer cannot merge a t-digest. Gating it would leave the free tier with no correct percentile at all, not a smaller one — the Crippleware Test's second question, answered as plainly as it ever is.
- **gravix CLI** — Operating the system from a terminal is baseline function.

### Borderline cases, decided in advance

- **Custom saved dashboards** — Charter §7.3 Q1 = yes — any team notices this missing.
- **Data export, manual and scheduled** — Export is the anti-lock-in guarantee; gating it is hostage-taking.
- **Local immutable audit log** — Baseline security control. Charter §7.3 Q3 = yes, so it cannot be sold.
- **Per-tenant rate limiting** — A safety control that protects the system, not a feature that gates users.
- **Public metrics API** — Reading your own data is not a premium feature. Charter §7.3 Q5 = yes.
- **Single-organisation RBAC, API keys, 2FA and sessions** — Charter §7.3 Q3 — charging for the ability to not be breached is the pattern the charter prevents.
- **Statistical deviation detection** — Shipped open in Horizon 1 Phase 2.5. Charter §7.3 Q4 makes that permanent.

## What we will never charge for

```
We will never charge for:

  - reading your own data, by API, by SQL, or by export;
  - getting your data out, in an open format, at any volume;
  - authentication, RBAC, two-factor, TLS, or audit logging;
  - the number of services, hosts, seats, or events you monitor;
  - how long you keep your own data on your own disk;
  - the correctness of any number Gravix reports.

These are not current pricing decisions. Charter §7.3 makes them structural: a
feature that fails the Crippleware Test cannot be sold, and a capability already
released under Apache-2.0 can never be taken back.

In Phase 7 we removed the paywall from five features that were already shipping
behind one — the public metrics API, custom dashboards, scheduled exports,
per-tenant rate limiting, and the audit log. That cost us revenue we already had.
It is the clearest evidence we can offer that the rule is real.
```

## What Gravix Pro adds

11 capabilities, each solving a problem that appears at a scale a single team does not
reach. None of them is a limit imposed on anything in the free list.

- **Continuous sync to an external data warehouse** — Operational convenience for a data team; the underlying Parquet is already freely exportable.
  <br/>*Built by GRVX-1311. Q5 is `no` because one-shot export stays core and complete (data-export): what is sold is the scheduling and the revision reconciliation, not the data. The package's own README opens by naming the free alternative, and its acceptance test compares what it would send against what `gravix export` produces, row for row — which is how F-046 was found.*
- **Cross-tenant fleet provisioning and lifecycle automation** — Operating many tenants' lifecycles from one console is running Gravix for other people, not a capability a single team needs.
  <br/>*Not yet implemented. GRVX-1304 builds it under ee/tenancy/; path updates then.*
- **Custom domains and signed embeddable dashboards** — Reselling Gravix under another brand is a go-to-market choice, not a baseline need.
  <br/>*Not yet implemented. GRVX-1310 builds it under ee/whitelabel/; path updates then. Narrows tenant-branding above to the two capabilities GRVX-1310 actually ships; basic per-tenant branding remains core.*
- **Managing N separate Gravix installations from one console** — Only an operator running many installations needs this; a single install has nothing to manage.
  <br/>*Built by GRVX-1307. Q1 stays `no` because a managed install is fully operable with the console absent — permanently, not for a grace period — so a team with one install loses nothing by not having this.*
- **Metering, Stripe billing and invoicing** — Only needed when charging other people for the service you run for them.
  <br/>*Not yet implemented. GRVX-1305 builds it; path updates then.*
- **Multi-tenant control plane** — Solves running Gravix for other people, which a single team never does.
  <br/>*Not yet implemented. GRVX-1304 builds it; path updates then.*
- **Non-Stripe manual/PO invoicing and consolidated cross-tenant statements** — Enterprise procurement workflows outside Stripe are a scale problem, not a correctness or security one.
  <br/>*Not yet implemented. GRVX-1305 builds it under ee/billing/; path updates then.*
- **SCIM v2 user provisioning and directory sync** — SCIM only matters with an enterprise IdP and headcount churn — a 10-person team using SSO does not miss it.
  <br/>*Not yet implemented. GRVX-1306 builds it under ee/identity/; path updates then. SAML and OIDC single sign-on itself stays core (rbac-single-org, charter §7.3 Q3): only directory provisioning is ee.*
- **SIEM log streaming, proactive retention-hold archival, SOC2 evidence packs** — The local audit log is already free and complete; streaming it to a SIEM and packaging auditor evidence only matters once a compliance team demands it.
  <br/>*Not yet implemented. GRVX-1308 builds it under ee/compliance/; path updates then. The audit log itself is core (audit-log-local) and stays complete: this is delivery to somebody else's system, not access to your own records.*
- **Seasonal forecasting and capacity projection** — Additive analysis over the same free warehouse data; its absence makes no displayed number less accurate.
  <br/>*Built by GRVX-1309. Q2 is `no` only because forecasting adds a projection alongside the measured numbers; if it ever changed a displayed measurement, it would be core. The free 2σ anomaly detector stays in the core untouched (§7.3 Q4), and ee/intelligence asserts that its evaluator and tests are still there.*
- **White-label branding, custom domains and embeds** — Only matters when reselling Gravix under your own brand.
  <br/>*Basic tenant branding shipped Apache-2.0 in Horizon 1 and stays core; only custom domains, embeds and full theming are ee (GRVX-1310).*

## Pricing

**No plans are defined yet, and this page will not invent them.**

Packaging and prices come from GRVX-1305, which is blocked: it depends on GRVX-1304, which
needs a new core extension point, and that is a design-tier change requiring **two maintainer
approvals** under `GOVERNANCE.md`. The project currently has one maintainer. RFC 0002 is drafted
and open.

What is already fixed, and will not change when plans are defined:

- The unit is **events ingested**, flat. No cardinality-driven pricing — Gravix's own criticism
  of cardinality billing applies to Gravix.
- Every plan will state its included volume and its overage rate **before** any signup step.
- No plan will impose a limit on any capability in the free list above.
- The full price will be on this page. No "contact us" for a listed tier, and no email gate.

## What happens if you stop paying

The core is unaffected. It does not phone home, it does not check a licence, and it does not
change behaviour when a subscription lapses — `ee/` is a separate directory the core is proven to
build without.

Your `ee/` configuration stays readable and exportable, and **nothing is deleted**. A lapsed
subscription removes access to `ee/` capabilities; it does not hold your data hostage, because
getting your data out is on the never-charge list above.

## Why the free tier is not a trial

A trial is a full product with a timer. This is a smaller product with no timer, and the
difference is enforced rather than promised:

- [The charter](https://github.com/lgreene03/gravix-dashboards/blob/main/docs/oss/00-open-core-charter.md)
  §7.1 requires the core to build, test and run with `ee/` physically deleted. CI does exactly
  that on every pull request.
- The **Crippleware Test** (§7.3) asks five questions of any proposed paid feature. All five must
  be "no". "People would pay for it" is never sufficient.
- GRVX-710 applied that test retroactively and moved five already-paid features into the free
  tier. The record for each is in `boundary.yaml` under `Gate removed by GRVX-710`.

There is no upsell anywhere in the product. An `ee/` capability you have not bought is **absent**,
not locked, not greyed out, and not advertised — charter §7.4, checked by a test.
